findings.text: The importer gate log named in the manifest's test_logs ends mid-progress at 26% with no pytest summary and no EXIT= line, so the 268 passed / 1 failed result it is cited for is not readable from the log; the figures are recoverable only from the worker's stream (resume-1.jsonl carries '1 failed, 268 passed, 1 warning in 355.92s'), and the log is also mislabelled as revision eca23f33d2 while its mtime is the run's own end at 23:28:51Z. Re-run the importer arm to a log that reaches its summary line, since a promotion receipt that reads this path finds an unread status.

The fragment states 'four more tests pass at head than at base', but the counts it gives either side (261 passed at base, 268 passed at head) are seven more passing; four is the number of tests the file gained. Say 'four more tests exist and pass at head, and the three base failures and errors now pass' so the recorded delta matches the numbers beside it.

The case asserts 'new_inode != first_inode' after unlinking and recreating the lock file; a filesystem that reuses the freed inode would red this case on correct code. The assertion it exists to support, recorded_service_lock_inode(...) == new_inode at :317) reads new_inode from the live file, so the guard does not depend on this inequality; deriving an expected differ or skipping when the inode is reused would keep the case stable.
